items.followUp: How is the magnitude and direction of a vector shown in a diagram?

rubric.why: Identifies the graphical form used to represent a vector.
rubric.description: A vector is represented by a directed line segment with an arrowhead.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is shown as a directed line segment or arrow.

rubric.why: Shows how the diagram represents the vector’s magnitude and direction.
rubric.description: The length represents magnitude (according to a scale), and the arrowhead shows direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly relating length to magnitude and arrowhead to direction.

modelAnswer: A vector quantity is represented graphically by a directed line segment or an arrow.
Its length represents its magnitude according to a scale, and its arrowhead shows its direction.

rubric.why: Checks the definition and scalar nature of speed.
rubric.description: Speed is distance travelled per unit time; it is a scalar quantity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the distance-per-time definition, with scalar nature accepted as supporting detail.

rubric.why: Checks the definition and directional nature of velocity.
rubric.description: Velocity is displacement per unit time in a particular direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the displacement-per-time definition and reference to direction.

modelAnswer: Speed is the distance travelled by a body per unit time; it is a scalar quantity.
Velocity is the displacement of a body per unit time in a particular direction.

items.followUp: Define a scalar quantity and give one example.

rubric.why: Checks the defining features of a vector quantity.
rubric.description: A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a vector has magnitude and direction.

rubric.why: Checks that the student can identify a valid vector example.
rubric.description: A valid example is force, velocity, displacement, or acceleration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct example.

modelAnswer: A physical quantity that has both magnitude and direction is called a vector quantity.
For example, force is a vector quantity.

items.followUp: State two properties of the action and reaction forces in Newton’s third law.

rubric.why: Checks the relative magnitudes and directions of the forces.
rubric.description: Action and reaction are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both equality and opposite direction.

rubric.why: Checks that the forces act on separate bodies.
rubric.description: Action and reaction act simultaneously on two different bodies.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they act on different bodies.

modelAnswer: Action and reaction are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.
They act simultaneously on two different bodies.

items.followUp: What is sliding friction, and how does it compare with rolling friction?

rubric.description: Rolling friction is less than sliding friction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating the comparison.

rubric.why: Checks the physical explanation for the smaller rolling friction.
rubric.description: During rolling, the body turns over the surface rather than continuously sliding across it, so the opposing friction is smaller.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that rolling involves less sliding or less deformation/interlocking at the contact.

modelAnswer: Rolling friction is less than sliding friction.
During rolling, the body turns over the surface instead of continuously sliding across it, so the opposing friction is smaller.

items.followUp: Give an example each of like and unlike parallel forces.

rubric.why: Checks the definition of like parallel forces.
rubric.description: Like parallel forces are parallel forces acting in the same direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they act in the same direction.

rubric.why: Checks the definition of unlike parallel forces.
rubric.description: Unlike parallel forces are parallel forces acting in opposite directions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they act in opposite directions.

modelAnswer: Like parallel forces are parallel forces that act in the same direction.
Unlike parallel forces are parallel forces that act in opposite directions.

items.followUp: State the conditions for a body to be in equilibrium.

rubric.why: Checks the condition for translational equilibrium.
rubric.description: The resultant force on the body is zero.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the net or resultant force is zero.

rubric.why: Checks the condition for rotational equilibrium.
rubric.description: The resultant torque on the body is zero.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the net torque is zero, or that clockwise and anticlockwise moments balance.

modelAnswer: A body is in equilibrium when the resultant force acting on it is zero.
For complete equilibrium, the resultant torque on it must also be zero.

items.followUp: What is the axis of rotation of a rotating wheel?

rubric.why: Checks that the axis is identified as a line.
rubric.description: The axis of rotation is a line.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a line (or imaginary line).

rubric.description: It is the line around which a body rotates.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the body rotates about this line.

modelAnswer: The axis of rotation is the line around which a body rotates.
